phases.name: Pure classifier, declared column, and the column reaching both targets

steps.name: Pure classifier: normaliser, ordered family table, first-match classification
criteria: Every golden title (45 generic titles, the nine contested cases and the double-qualifier titles included) is classified into the ratified family, and every title no pattern matches is classified other
Case, punctuation, spacing, accent and symbol variants of a title reach the same family as the plain title; a pattern never matches inside a longer word

Where a title holds phrases of two families, the earlier family in the ratified order wins (agile coach, scrum master, AI transformation, transformation/change, engineering/delivery manager, product/product ops)

Any input is classified without throwing: empty, blank, punctuation-only, non-text (including symbol, bigint, function), other scripts and very long titles all yield one member of the closed set, and normalising anything that is not text gives the empty string

The family table is a frozen ordered list of frozen descriptors: the six ratified families in the ratified order, other not a descriptor, no repeated family, no empty or non-normalised pattern, no pattern held twice, no pattern shadowed by an earlier one, every pattern exercised by a golden title that lands in its family

The 13 classification and normalisation properties hold over generated input: total and closed, deterministic, normalising twice is normalising once, invariance under case, whitespace, separators and accents, priority, first-match oracle, whole words only, fallback, reachability
src/core/role-families.mjs imports nothing, declares no class, mutates nothing and uses no node: builtin; npm run check:arch stays green

steps.name: Declare the Role Family column and fill it in a newly built workbook
criteria: WALKING-SKELETON PRECONDITION: a newly built workbook carries Role Family immediately after Fit Reason, holds one family per advert, and the family is the golden family for the title

Role Family is in the Jobs header and is harvester-owned: never human-owned, never the key; the Jobs header is still Dedup Key plus harvester-owned plus human-owned columns as a set with no column named twice (the drift guard that holds today keeps holding)
The Jobs header has 27 names; the legacy 26-name header is exactly the old one, so a tracker predating the column needs a wider grid
Every Jobs row from a harvest carries Role Family under every declared Jobs column and none other, filled from the advert's title alone

A rebuild from a directory of cached alerts carries the column too, and one advert surfaced by two saved searches, retitled between sightings, or reposted under new job ids has the family the row's first-sighting title gives, whatever the company, search or arrival order
A very long title, a punctuation-only title and a title in a script no pattern uses are written with their family (other where nothing matches)

The one human-approved edit to an existing test is made and no other: the expected columnCount in tests/acceptance/sheets-api-target/sheets-fake.test.mjs line 55 changes from 26 to 27, nothing else in that file; every other existing test passes unmodified (if any other existing test fails, stop and report it instead of editing it)

steps.name: The column reaches existing trackers: xlsx merge, dry-run and the Sheets target
criteria: xlsx merge: Role Family is appended at the far right of the last existing header cell, every matched row is filled, and every human cell, unknown column, other tab and hand-added row without a Dedup Key is byte-identical

The first population is not itemised: stdout counts the appended column, stderr says no derived corrections, the report file holds nothing about it; a later re-classification is itemised one line per changed advert and the unchanged adverts are not mentioned

A family the operator typed over the harvester's, and a Role Family column the operator created by hand (even moved beside Status), is overwritten or filled where it stands as a harvester-owned column, with each changed cell itemised and nothing appended
A second build against an up-to-date tracker changes no cell, itemises no correction, appends no column and, on the Sheets target, sends no batch at all
--dry-run on xlsx names the column it would append and the cell changes, and the workspace is byte-identical afterwards

Sheets target: the whole change is one batch inside the four allowed request kinds (updateCells, appendCells, appendDimension, addSheet) writing only the Role Family column; the header cell is written at the old header width, with a widening of the grid when it is exactly as wide as the old header, none when a spare column exists, and after any human column that lies between
About 3,050 adverts are written in one batch within the size limit and none is refused as too large; a Sheet naming Role Family twice is refused as sheets.duplicate-header with nothing written
Every existing xlsx, Sheets and Gmail scenario passes unmodified

phases.name: Tuning view of the most frequent other titles

steps.name: Tuning summary and the stderr tuning view on merge, Sheets and dry-run builds
criteria: WALKING SKELETON: build --target sheets against a tracker that predates the column fills Role Family for every advert, leaves the operator's Status and notes untouched, itemises no correction for the first population, and names the one advert that fell through in the tuning view

The summary of Jobs rows returns the row total, the count per family and the most frequent other titles as normalised title and count, ordered by count descending then title ascending, cut at the limit (a limit of 0 gives an empty list while still counting), grouping titles that differ only in case, punctuation and spacing, never listing a title of another family, giving an empty list when no advert is other, giving a summary of nothing for no adverts, and never changing the rows it is handed

Its properties hold over generated rows: family counts add up to the total and the other count is the number of other adverts; the list is at most the limit, ordered, and never counts more adverts than fell through; with room for every title the list accounts for every advert that fell through; the order of the adverts never changes the summary

A merge build, a Sheets build, and --dry-run with or without --merge print on stderr after the change summary a counts line containing 'role families' and, for each family present, the family and its count, then 'harvest build: <n> of <total> advert(s) classified other; most frequent:' followed by at most 15 lines of the form count then normalised title; the 16th and later titles are cut
The whole view, counts line included, is omitted when no advert is other; the view never appears on stdout and never in the --report file, so an empty report still means nothing changed
--dry-run still returns a plan and writes nothing: the workspace is byte-identical, the Sheets fake records no write request, and no write capability is constructed
A title that falls through is shown from the very first preview of a tracker that lacks the column, and that preview with no tracker plans every advert as a new row and writes no file

phases.name: Scale check and retiring the RED scaffold

steps.name: Operator-run scale check: about 3,050 single-cell updates plus an appended header on a 26-column grid
criteria: The check is operator-run only, is not part of npm test, and the script passes node --check and its existing offline --self-test against the loopback fake, with the new check included in the self-test
The check imports no tracker of the operator's: it builds a synthetic Jobs tab on a scratch Sheet whose grid is exactly 26 columns wide, with about 3,050 rows

It sends about 3,050 single-cell updates plus the appended Role Family header and the grid-widening request in one spreadsheets.batchUpdate, and reports whether the request count was accepted, the response status and the payload size
It deletes the scratch Sheet it created, even when the check fails, and deletes only that id
It prints a result row that can be pasted back, containing no token, client secret or unredacted id; bodies it saves are redacted as the existing script redacts them
The crafter does NOT run the check live (no credentials are available): the step ends at the offline self-test

steps.implementation_notes: Implements OQ-7 (ratified 2026-10-02). Extend scripts/sheets-live-check.mjs as a new named check beside the existing ones, reusing its redaction, scratch-Sheet provisioning and deletion, VERDICT and result-table helpers; keep the existing parseArgs usage working (the check should be selectable with --only and appear in the full run) and keep --self-test green.
